normalized_hits.abstract: This study presents an extension of the conventional data warehouse query paradigm by introducing Multi-dimensional Graph eXpression (MGX), a multidimensional query framework designed to support Online Analytical Processing (OLAP) over graph-based business intelligence data. MGX extends the traditional Multi-Dimensional eXpression (MDX) syntax used in relational data warehouses by incorporating SQL-style analytical constructs, including GROUP BY, HAVING, and ORDER BY, thereby improving the expressive capability and flexibility of multidimensional analysis over graph warehouses. By bridging relational data warehousing technologies with graph-based analytical environments, the proposed framework addresses key limitations of traditional MDX in supporting graph-oriented analytics. It enables more effective exploration of semantically rich and socially connected knowledge embedded in networked datasets. Overall, MGX provides a practical methodological foundation for advancing graph warehousing and supporting next-generation network-centric business intelligence applications.

normalized_hits.abstract: Drug-Drug Interactions (DDIs) often cause significant adverse events, making early identification crucial, especially with rising polypharmacy. While most methods focus on binary prediction, multiclass DDI prediction is more advantageous as it identifies specific interaction types. However, this is challenging due to class imbalance, with many rare interaction types compared to dominant ones. We propose a multiclass DDI prediction framework comprising three components: Stage 1 involves feature extraction, where the molecular structures of two drugs are modeled as graphs using a graph attention network (GAT) as an encoder, then combined with Drug Repurposing Knowledge Graph (DRKG) embeddings to produce enhanced drug features. Stage 2 involves expert modelling, where the paired drug representations are processed by two Mamba State Space Model (SSM)- based experts: a standard Mamba expert and a class-reweighted Mamba expert, which efficiently capture sequential dependencies and interaction patterns between the drug representations. Stage 3 involves gated fusion, where a confidence-based gating strategy integrates the two experts to generate final predictions. The performance on DrugBank and DDIMDL benchmark datasets achieved macro F1 scores of 90.68% and 83.99%, demonstrating our framework’s effectiveness in multiclass DDI prediction. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/devalab/MambaDDI .

normalized_hits.abstract: For deep learning-based object identification systems to be more accurate and efficient, feature selection is essential. High-dimensional feature spaces frequently contain redundant or unnecessary data, which raises the danger of overfitting and increases computational expense. In this work, we compare two widely used nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithms for feature reduction in deep learning pipelines: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). In order to find an ideal subset of features that maximizes classification performance while minimizing dimensionality, the suggested method combines a pre-trained convolutional neural network (CNN) for feature extraction, PSO, and GWO. Benchmark image datasets are used for extensive experimentation, and the accuracy, F1-score, computational complexity, and convergence behavior of the findings are assessed. Both PSO and GWO considerably reduce the feature set size without compromising model performance, according to our findings, with PSO exhibiting higher robustness and faster convergence in high-dimensional search spaces. This work proposes a scalable approach for real-world object recognition problems and sheds light on the practical trade-offs of swarm intelligence-based optimizers for feature selection.

normalized_hits.abstract: Contemporary CI/CD practices typically address vulnerability prevention and intrusion mitigation as disjoint activities, which may result in residual risk even after container images pass pre-deployment checks. Pre-deployment scanners can overlook vulnerabilities obscured by image layering or insufficient metadata, whereas runtime detection mechanisms commonly rely on single-source observations and thus fail to capture multi-step exploit chains. This work presents Janus , a coordinated framework for containerized CI/CD security across the pre- and post-deployment phases. Its key idea is that vulnerabilities should be handled according to when they can be addressed most effectively: Janus uses a policy gate to decide which vulnerabilities must be remediated before release and which residual vulnerabilities are explicitly deferred to runtime monitoring. To support pre-deployment decisions under CI/CD time budgets, Janus performs layer-aware incremental scanning and policy-controlled constrained patching on changed image layers. To protect against residual risk after deployment, it enforces the deferred set using abstract, stateful exploit-chain signatures that correlate system and network events through shallow-to-deep runtime inspection. Our evaluation on 346 container images (including all 146 official and 200 widely used community images) shows that Janus improves vulnerability coverage by 42.4% relative to representative scanners in our setup (e.g., Grype, Trivy, CVE-Bin-Tool) while reducing analysis latency by 79.6%. Moreover, on our tested exploit chains, Janus detects all chains that elude representative single-source IDS baselines. These results demonstrate the benefits of coordinating prevention and mitigation across the container lifecycle.

normalized_hits.abstract: Predicting drug-drug interactions (DDIs) on biomedical knowledge graphs is often biased toward high-degree drugs: under standard training they receive more message passing and gradient updates than low-degree drugs, skewing optimization. We call this a computational Matthew effect (cumulative advantage in optimization only; not a claim about patients or prescribers). FairTIGER encodes each drug with a molecular Graph Transformer and a local KG-subgraph Transformer, and targets degree-related training imbalance with (1) degree-aware attention biases, and (2) loss reweighting that up-weights pairs involving low-degree drugs. Optional mutual information terms keep fused embeddings aligned with local node features. We evaluate with standard global classification metrics (ACC, F1, AUC, AUPR) on DrugBank, KEGG, and OGB-biokg, where FairTIGER improves over competitive baselines overall, including dual-channel TIGER variants; degree-stratified evaluation is left to future work.

normalized_hits.abstract: The increasing prevalence of polypharmacy has made drug-drug interactions (DDIs) a critical concern for medication safety. Existing computational approaches exhibit two limitations: most rely on a single feature source or static-weight concatenation, and side-effect data are frequently incomplete, yet few methods address robust prediction under partial modality absence. To improve the modeling of complex pharmacological relationships, this study introduces SEAR-DDI, a side effect aware multi-source representation learning architecture for DDI prediction. The framework jointly exploits four modalities (molecular graph structures, molecular fingerprints, knowledge graph embeddings, and side-effect profiles) into a unified 128-dimensional space and fuses them through a four-modal self-attention module that learns inter-modal importance weights for each drug pair. Evaluated on the DrugBank 86-class benchmark, SEAR-DDI achieves 96.14% accuracy, 92.38% macro-averaged F1, and 96.02% weighted F1, outperforming all compared baselines. Ablation experiments validate the significance of each modality and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed multi-modal attention fusion strategy.

normalized_hits.abstract: Knowledge Graph Embeddings are widely used to represent structured knowledge and support intelligent decision-making systems. While their effectiveness has been demonstrated for link prediction, their suitability for other tasks, such as semantic similarity, remains insufficiently explored, particularly with regarding transparency, user trust, and alignment with human expectations. This research extends an existing system with two objectives: i) assessing the ability of Knowledge Graph Embedding Models to capture semantic information in similarity tasks; ii) improving the readability and fluency of explanations describing shared properties among nearby resources. This enables a clearer understanding of whether Knowledge Graph Embedding Models are effective beyond link prediction. Furthermore, the work investigates whether incorporating user feedback into the embedding refinement process can align similarity outcomes with user expectations and domain-specific needs. The proposed approaches promote a symbiotic AI paradigm, improving semantic adequacy and contributing to more explainable, adaptive, and human-centered AI.

normalized_hits.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce websites has caused the number of customer reviews to rapidly increase, making the analysis of such reviews more challenging than ever before. Existing approaches to summarizing the content of customer reviews primarily focus on lexical similarity while paying little attention to product aspect preservation, sentiment alignment, and redundant information filtering. In this work, we propose a Sentiment-Aware Redundancy-Minimized Maximum Marginal Relevance (SA-RMMR) framework for creating informative extractive summaries that can preserve product aspects, customer sentiments, and informational diversity. Our framework relies on SBERT-based semantic representation of text, TF-IDF and part-of-speech-based aspect extraction, VADER-based sentiment alignment, and a redundancy-aware maximum marginal relevance ranking. In order to make our framework robust, we introduce semantic centrality estimation, adaptive retrieval confidence, reward mixing, and balance adjustment. The quality of the created summaries is estimated with conventional lexical metrics and a new metric called Composite Quality Index (CQI) that jointly evaluates semantic relevance, aspect coverage, sentiment alignment, and redundancies. We performed experiments on several Amazon product reviews datasets and have shown that our framework was the best among all methods considered in the experiment, obtaining the highest Aspect Coverage (0.835) and Sentiment Alignment (0.719) scores while having competitive semantic similarity (BERTScore-F1 = 0.825). Our framework significantly outperformed classical extractive approaches and transformer-based models, including BART, PEGASUS, and FLAN-T5, in overall quality of summaries produced by them. Ablation studies showed that semantic representation of sentences, aspect awareness, adaptive retrieval, and redundancy elimination all have positive impact on performance of the framework. The proposed SA-RMMR framework represents an efficient and interpretable approach to customer review summarization that takes into account not only semantic relevance but also product aspects, sentiment preservation, and redundant information filtering. Additionally, the proposed Composite Quality Index allows evaluation of the quality of summaries from multiple perspectives, not limited to conventional lexical overlap, which makes it a good choice for opinion mining tasks in e-commerce.

We call this a computational Matthew effect (cumulative advantage in optimization only; not a claim about patients or prescribers). FairTIGER encodes each drug with a molecular Graph Transformer and a local KG-subgraph Transformer, and targets degree-related training imbalance with (1) degree-aware attention biases, and (2) loss reweighting that up-weights pairs involving low-degree drugs. Optional mutual information terms keep fused embeddings aligned with local node features. We evaluate with standard global classification metrics (ACC, F1, AUC, AUPR) on DrugBank, KEGG, and OGB-biokg, where FairTIGER improves over competitive baselines overall, including dual-channel TIGER variants; degree-stratified evaluation is left to future work.

raw_result.abstract: The increasing prevalence of polypharmacy has made drug-drug interactions (DDIs) a critical concern for medication safety. Existing computational approaches exhibit two limitations: most rely on a single feature source or static-weight concatenation, and side-effect data are frequently incomplete, yet few methods address robust prediction under partial modality absence. To improve the modeling of complex pharmacological relationships, this study introduces SEAR-DDI, a side effect aware multi-source representation learning architecture for DDI prediction. The framework jointly exploits four modalities (molecular graph structures, molecular fingerprints, knowledge graph embeddings, and side-effect profiles) into a unified 128-dimensional space and fuses them through a four-modal self-attention module that learns inter-modal importance weights for each drug pair. Evaluated on the DrugBank 86-class benchmark, SEAR-DDI achieves 96.14% accuracy, 92.38% macro-averaged F1, and 96.02% weighted F1, outperforming all compared baselines. Ablation experiments validate the significance of each modality and demonstrate the superiority of the proposed multi-modal attention fusion strategy.

raw_result.abstract: Knowledge Graph Embeddings are widely used to represent structured knowledge and support intelligent decision-making systems. While their effectiveness has been demonstrated for link prediction, their suitability for other tasks, such as semantic similarity, remains insufficiently explored, particularly with regarding transparency, user trust, and alignment with human expectations. This research extends an existing system with two objectives: i) assessing the ability of Knowledge Graph Embedding Models to capture semantic information in similarity tasks; ii) improving the readability and fluency of explanations describing shared properties among nearby resources. This enables a clearer understanding of whether Knowledge Graph Embedding Models are effective beyond link prediction. Furthermore, the work investigates whether incorporating user feedback into the embedding refinement process can align similarity outcomes with user expectations and domain-specific needs. The proposed approaches promote a symbiotic AI paradigm, improving semantic adequacy and contributing to more explainable, adaptive, and human-centered AI.

raw_result.abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce websites has caused the number of customer reviews to rapidly increase, making the analysis of such reviews more challenging than ever before. Existing approaches to summarizing the content of customer reviews primarily focus on lexical similarity while paying little attention to product aspect preservation, sentiment alignment, and redundant information filtering. In this work, we propose a Sentiment-Aware Redundancy-Minimized Maximum Marginal Relevance (SA-RMMR) framework for creating informative extractive summaries that can preserve product aspects, customer sentiments, and informational diversity. Our framework relies on SBERT-based semantic representation of text, TF-IDF and part-of-speech-based aspect extraction, VADER-based sentiment alignment, and a redundancy-aware maximum marginal relevance ranking. In order to make our framework robust, we introduce semantic centrality estimation, adaptive retrieval confidence, reward mixing, and balance adjustment. The quality of the created summaries is estimated with conventional lexical metrics and a new metric called Composite Quality Index (CQI) that jointly evaluates semantic relevance, aspect coverage, sentiment alignment, and redundancies. We performed experiments on several Amazon product reviews datasets and have shown that our framework was the best among all methods considered in the experiment, obtaining the highest Aspect Coverage (0.835) and Sentiment Alignment (0.719) scores while having competitive semantic similarity (BERTScore-F1 = 0.825). Our framework significantly outperformed classical extractive approaches and transformer-based models, including BART, PEGASUS, and FLAN-T5, in overall quality of summaries produced by them. Ablation studies showed that semantic representation of sentences, aspect awareness, adaptive retrieval, and redundancy elimination all have positive impact on performance of the framework. The proposed SA-RMMR framework represents an efficient and interpretable approach to customer review summarization that takes into account not only semantic relevance but also product aspects, sentiment preservation, and redundant information filtering. Additionally, the proposed Composite Quality Index allows evaluation of the quality of summaries from multiple perspectives, not limited to conventional lexical overlap, which makes it a good choice for opinion mining tasks in e-commerce.
